papers.title: Kernel-based stochastic collocation for the random two-phase Navier-Stokes equations
papers.abstract: In this work, we apply stochastic collocation methods with radial kernel basis functions for an uncertainty quantification of the random incompressible two-phase Navier-Stokes equations. Our approach is non-intrusive and we use the existing fluid dynamics solver NaSt3DGPF to solve the incompressible two-phase Navier-Stokes equation for each given realization. We are able to empirically show that the resulting kernel-based stochastic collocation is highly competitive in this setting and even outperforms some other standard methods.

summary_en.motivation: To quantify uncertainties in random incompressible two-phase Navier-Stokes equations using non-intrusive stochastic collocation.
summary_en.method: Radial kernel basis functions are employed in a stochastic collocation framework, leveraging an existing CFD solver for each realization.
summary_en.result: The kernel-based approach demonstrates competitive accuracy and outperforms standard methods in empirical tests.
summary_en.validation: Numerical benchmarks on two-phase flow problems are used to assess the method's performance.
